prompts.idle:
Use case: identity-preserve, precise proportion correction of an animation sprite atlas. Image 1 is the ORIGINAL B character whose body proportions the user selected. Image 2 is the remake atlas to edit. Keep Image 2's six poses, sharp simplified clothes, identity, colors, eye design and clean linework, but CORRECT its overlarge head and overwide body silhouette to match Image 1. The remake currently has a head taking about 62% of total standing height; that is too large. Target crown/headband-to-chin height about 50–52% of full crown-to-shoes height, with the neck-to-shoes body taking the remaining 48–50%. The torso and legs should remain short and cute like ORIGINAL B, not a tall adult. Make the head noticeably smaller relative to the torso than Image 2, and overall hair/ear/tail silhouette less wide. Match the overall visible width-to-height ratio of original B about 0.74. Original B is the authority for proportions; Image 2 is only the authority for simplified style and action poses. Keep her unmistakable whale ear fins and whale tail, plain white scalloped headband, blue eyes, navy hair, one neck bow, plain navy dress, smooth white apron with a single blue whale emblem, white socks and navy shoes. No lace layers, embroidery, jewelry, extra frills, tiny buttons or gold details.
Layout must stay 1536 x 1024, THREE columns by TWO rows, exactly six frames, 512 x 512 equal cells. In every cell, whole character roughly 440 pixels high and no more than 335 pixels wide. Ground at local y=474; top at y=34; chin approximately y=255. Keep padding and transparent gaps. Same scale and identity across cells. Fixed anchors; no individual panel borders, labels, backgrounds or cast shadows. Actual transparent alpha, preserve it. Do not draw blue backdrops. No resampling or blurry upscaling: redraw corrected geometry with crisp edges.
Preserve the six front-facing idle phases in order: open eyes; gentle inhale; half blink; fully closed blink; reopen; neutral tiny tail sway. Keep feet and head anchor stationary.
